# Implementation status

Updated: 2026-10-10, local native core and private entry recovery gates passed; independent remote proof pending.

The runnable core includes distinct stable identities and execution generations, a private Unix-socket daemon, serialized SQLite registry/journal, durable operation and lease identity, isolated tmux lifecycle, inherited-nonce linking, and a Bubble Tea switcher with remembered selection/groups/drafts. Missing runtimes are retained as missing; they are not automatically relaunched.

Source `b962535ec785db1243b032d573e43dc1dafc73d9` passed `make build check` on macOS arm64 with Go 1.26.6, tmux 3.7b, Codex 0.159.0, and Claude 2.1.296. Both real programs were entered from the TUI, received unsubmitted Unicode drafts, detached to the same selection, and survived a daemon restart with exact execution/runtime identity. The restart experiment exposed a leaked lock descriptor; the fix and an actual surviving-child regression are included in that SHA. [Core evidence](../evidence/2026-10-10-core-integration.md).

`4bf0162` adds a passing daemon race test for a delayed old stop after a synthetic replacement execution. It proves stale command rejection at that boundary, not a native continuation feature.

Independent acceptance of implementation `4bf01620db4fad2994d245212a4fab9c05571c8f` passed eight groups covering native keys/resize, TUI and daemon SIGKILL, dropped launch/attach/stop responses, writer competition, nonce rejection, ten-session switching, missing-runtime retention and journal recovery. Two real programs and eight explicit fixture sessions were used. No model turn was submitted, and native account/model/thread attribution remains unknown. [Independent core evidence](../evidence/2026-10-10-independent-native-core.md). This receipt does not certify later gateway or setup changes.

Owned provider discovery, selected user/project skill installation and crash-safe removal are integrated. Removal retains the intact bundle and independent receipts in a private archive; there is no automatic purge. Native Codex catalogue discovery and Claude's `/backplane` selector discovery have been observed without skill invocation or model turns. [Claude discovery and removal evidence](../evidence/2026-10-10-claude-project-discovery.md).

Implementation `4b36f4d773a31388c7ec8ade146eb1929a8d2a19` passed the full build, race tests and vet. Linux amd64 cross-compilation passed; Linux runtime behavior remains untested. Independent native acceptance in checkout `498abebbd69f99bff9bb7542bac37a6815d71c5d`, with an empty implementation diff to that frozen SHA, passed all eight local groups and both-provider gateway journeys. Codex and Claude received unsubmitted Unicode, resize and Escape, detached to the actual TUI with exact release, and reconnected to the same execution/PID/pane. The initial Codex timeout was a readiness predicate missing the observed `»` composer glyph; preserved receipts and the minimal harness correction qualify the rerun. [Current native evidence](../evidence/2026-10-10-independent-repaired-native.md).

The executable private gateway and client companion now retain original acquisition authority across lost acknowledgement and entry restart, hide home runtime locators, project current grants and keep healthy work usable when a home is unavailable. The reproduced authority, revocation and blocked-output defects were repaired. The adverse executable authority cases and all six gateway fixture groups passed against frozen `4b36f4d`; independent review found no remaining blocker in those repaired boundaries. [Gateway gate](../evidence/2026-10-10-gateway-hardened.md). One directory invocation returned healthy partial inventory in 3.009835 seconds while an owned home daemon was stopped, and the actual TUI still attached/input/detached at the healthy home. [Silent-home evidence](../evidence/2026-10-10-gateway-silent-home-latency.md). These are two execution homes on one physical computer. Independent second-server authentication/enrollment and the real SSH host/workspace selection remain pending.

Codex 0.159.0 also joined an owned idle app-server native thread from two initialized connections with zero turns. That feasibility result exposes no native writer lease; a scoped broker with durable writer fencing is the next semantic-adapter boundary. It is not an implemented semantic capability. [Zero-turn study](../research/CODEX_SEMANTIC_SPIKE.md).

The separate experimental `codex/codex-broker` branch contains a strict installed-version wire policy, a private Unix-WebSocket relay and a durable actor sharing the existing writer reservation. Policy unit acceptance and direct installed app-server wire proof passed independently. The actor integration passed source build/race/vet, but independent review reproduced handover callback timing and damaged-reservation gaps; repairs are in progress. Counted relay fixtures exposed malformed-source recovery that also needs a durable blocker. The real native helper proved owned process/socket identity and durable exact-thread resume before stopping on a pinned envelope incompatibility. This branch is not accepted or privately pushed yet and advertises no semantic capability. [Authority source qualification](../evidence/2026-10-10-codex-authority.md), [policy evidence](../evidence/2026-10-10-codex-policy.md), [direct wire evidence](../evidence/2026-10-10-codex-wire.md).

Planned/not run: authenticated model-turn evidence, verified account/model/native-thread attribution, real second-server acceptance, semantic Mattermost/IRC delivery, shared repairs/meters, subscription routing, native continuity, and optional captains. No public release or deployment has occurred. The repository remains private.
